title: System-wide failure catalog and error telemetry work
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Teams lack a single, queryable catalog of failure modes combined with trace-enriched telemetry to reliably differentiate timeouts, overload, model-level failures, and transport errors (HTTP/gRPC codes). This ticket scopes the implementation of a canonical failure taxonomy, the enrichment pipeline for traces/metrics/logs, and a set of drillable dashboards and incident playbooks for on-call and SRE teams.

We will: 1) define taxonomy and canonical labels for failures, 2) instrument trace hooks and span tags at layer boundaries, 3) transform logs/metrics to attach taxonomy tags, and 4) build latency/error dashboards with linked trace drilldowns, Sankey-style request flows, and a failure fingerprint index for triage and regression detection.
background: Multiple recent incidents exposed inconsistent labeling across the serving runtime, API gateway, and model adapter. Current diagnostic workflows rely on ad-hoc logs and handcrafted dashboards that make it hard to measure request-level failure rates across model variants and routing policies. Aligns with Observability 2025 objectives to reduce MTTR and improve regression detection for inference failures.
goals: Ship a documented failure taxonomy covering timeouts, overload, model errors, grpc/http status ranges, tokenization/serialization errors, and internal runtime panics
Produce an enrichment pipeline that attaches failure_tag, failure_reason, and rule_id to traces and logs within 100ms of ingestion
Deliver interactive dashboards with top-N failure drivers, per-model and per-route heatmaps, and trace-linked drilldowns
Enable alerting rules and automated runbooks for high-severity failure fingerprints
success_metrics: MTTR for P0 inference incidents reduced by 30% within one release window
False-positive alert rate for inference errors reduced by 40% after taxonomy rollout
Baseline coverage: >=95% of production traffic annotated with a taxonomy label in traces/logs
acceptance_criteria: Canonical taxonomy document published and approved by SRE, Runtime, and API teams
Telemetry pipeline pushes enriched events to the observability backend under fields 'redwood.failure.tag' and 'redwood.failure.reason'
Dashboard templates (Latency by Failure Tag, Failure Sankey, Failure Fingerprints) available in Console and shareable via link
Playbook templates created for top 6 fingerprinted failures with runbook steps and escalation paths
End-to-end test that injects synthetic errors and asserts correct taxonomy labeling and dashboard visibility
milestones: M2: Trace hook changes merged to runtime adapters + feature flag (2025-02-28)
M3: Enrichment pipeline schema + transform job deployed to staging (2025-03-07)
M4: Dashboards implemented and integrated with trace links (2025-03-18)
M6: Full rollout and runbooks published (2025-03-25)
tech_notes: Taxonomy will map broad classes: timeout.client, timeout.backend, overload.queue, overload.cpu, model.error.generation, model.error.tokenization, transport.http.4xx, transport.http.5xx, transport.grpc.unavailable, internal.oom, internal.panic

Instrumentation: add span attribute 'redwood.failure.info' and event 'redwood.failure.event' at boundary adapters (API gateway, route broker, model adapter). Use OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where possible.

Enrichment pipeline: source=otlp spans -> collector proc (tag enrichment) -> kafka topic -> transform job (flink) -> observability sink (ClickHouse for metrics, ES for logs, Jaeger/Tempo index for traces)
Fingerprinting: canonicalize stack traces, model error messages (regex normalization), and HTTP/grpc code + path combinations; store in fingerprint index with TTL 90d
Privacy: ensure no PII in failure_reason strings; add KMS-based redaction step for sensitive fields
Performance: enrichment must add <1% CPU overhead at the runtime boundary when feature-flag off; gradual rollout to avoid RPS impact
implementation_plan: 1) Taxonomy workshop with Runtime, SRE, API, and Product (lead: Marco Liu)
2) Patch gateway and model adapter to emit structured failure events with minimal blocking I/O
3) Deploy collector-based enrichment and validate in staging using synthetic traffic harness
4) Build Grafana/Console dashboards and link each row to trace explorer with prefilled query
5) Create automated smoke tests and synthetic canary suite that asserts taxonomy labels and alert firing
6) Run a 48-hour canary with 10% of traffic then expand to 100%
dashboards_spec: Overview: Time-series of error rate by failure_tag, 7d/1d/1h granularity
Failure Sankey: Source (gateway/runtime/model) -> failure_tag -> top routes/models
Latency by Failure Tag: P50/P90/P99 split by success vs failure tags
Fingerprint index viewer: list of fingerprints, last seen, severity, sample trace link
Drilldown: from any row open trace explorer with redwood.failure.* prefilled filters
runbooks: timeout.backend: Check model node busy / KV cache misses -> verify batch sizes and queue length -> scale target pool or fallback to async path
overload.queue: Throttle rules and token-bucket metrics -> evaluate autoscale metrics and deferred queue depths
model.error.generation: Snapshot input prompt, model version, and replication token -> open model-oncall runbook and capture sample trace
transport.http.5xx: Correlate gateway logs + backend trace spans and inspect upstream gRPC reasons
testing_plan: Synthetic traffic that injects timeouts at the backend and asserts 'timeout.backend' labeling
Chaos test that simulates node OOM and validates internal.oom fingerprinting
End-to-end staging run that validates dashboard queries and trace links for a representative subset of routes
risks: Mislabeling: overlapping failure conditions may create ambiguous tags; mitigation: layered rules with precedence and manual review
Telemetry volume growth: adding enrichment fields increases event payload; mitigation: field pruning and sampling policy
Performance regression in runtime adapters: mitigate via feature flags and incremental rollout
